title: RDS + Aurora deep dive
topic: RDS Multi-AZ, read replicas, Aurora storage and failover, Aurora Serverless v2, RDS Proxy, backups/RPO, DynamoDB vs relational for GSA stats
format: 15 timed scenario questions (~24 min, ~96 sec each). Reinforces night-15-rds-aurora.md. Answer without peeking at night-15-quiz-answers.json first.
answerDistribution: A×4 B×4 C×4 D×3 — options shuffled so correct letter varies

questions.question: Global Ski Atlas runs Aurora PostgreSQL as the production writer in us-east-1. Leadership wants automatic failover if the primary AZ fails with minimal write data loss and no manual DNS changes. Reports must not be routed to the standby during normal operation. What configuration fits?

options.A: Three cross-Region read replicas with Route 53 weighted routing pointed at all writer endpoints
options.B: Aurora read replica in a second AZ promoted automatically by EventBridge on failure
options.C: Aurora cluster with Multi-AZ writer failover — sync storage, automatic endpoint update
options.D: RDS Single-AZ with daily manual snapshots copied to a standby Region for disaster recovery

questions.question: A stats Lambda in the Night 9 VPC spikes to 2,000 concurrent executions after each Iceland completion message. Each invocation opens a new PostgreSQL connection to Aurora and you hit max_connections errors. The DB team wants pooling without rewriting application code. Best add-on?

options.A: ElastiCache Redis cluster in front of Aurora to cache connection strings for Lambda
options.B: Amazon RDS Proxy in the same VPC — multiplexes Lambda connections to the cluster
options.C: Aurora Global Database secondary in another Region to split connection load evenly
options.D: DynamoDB on-demand table replacing Aurora for all relational stats query workloads

questions.question: A dev-only GSA reporting database is queried heavily for two hours after each monthly Iceland run and sits idle the rest of the month. You want PostgreSQL compatibility with automatic capacity scaling and minimal ops. Cost when idle should be low but the instance may stay warm. Best engine?

options.A: Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL — scales ACUs with workload; minimum capacity still billed
options.B: RDS Oracle Multi-AZ — enterprise features sized for intermittent monthly reporting spikes
options.C: Aurora Serverless v1 — required today for any database that must scale fully to zero ACUs
options.D: Self-managed PostgreSQL on a large EC2 Reserved Instance left running continuously all month

questions.question: The GSA BI team runs heavy SELECT dashboards against resort aggregates. Write traffic to the primary must stay fast during month-end reporting. The primary is RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ in us-east-1. How do you scale reads without adding write load to the primary?

options.A: Enable Multi-AZ — the synchronous standby serves read-only analytics traffic by default always
options.B: Point dashboards at the Aurora cluster writer endpoint with read-only IAM database users only
options.C: Create an S3 Gateway Endpoint so reports read Iceberg files instead of running SQL queries
options.D: Add RDS read replicas — async copies dedicated to read-only dashboard and reporting queries

questions.question: GSA needs a secondary Region for disaster recovery with Aurora PostgreSQL. RPO must be under one second and secondary Region should serve read-only queries before a controlled failover. Which Aurora feature matches?

options.A: Cross-Region automated backup copy with 35-day retention and no live secondary reads
options.B: RDS read replica in eu-west-1 manually promoted after a Route 53 health check failure
options.C: Aurora Global Database — primary in us-east-1, secondary Region with sub-second lag
options.D: DynamoDB global tables with multi-Region eventually consistent reads for SQL reports

questions.question: The Night 13 SQS stats uploader must store resort rows, monthly aggregates, and foreign keys between resort_dimension and monthly_agg. Downstream SQL must JOIN tables for ad-hoc reports. Wiki visitor counters stay in DynamoDB. Where should the relational stats live?

options.A: DynamoDB with one GSI per JOIN pattern — avoids VPC networking for the stats uploader
options.B: Aurora PostgreSQL or RDS PostgreSQL — relational schema, JOINs, and ACID write batches
options.C: S3 Iceberg only — no database; Athena replaces all transactional updates and JOINs
options.D: ElastiCache Redis hashes — primary durable store for resort dimension and aggregate data

questions.question: An Aurora PostgreSQL cluster ingests Iceland metadata faster than forecast. CloudWatch shows storage growing but no DBA action was taken. A junior engineer proposes doubling provisioned Aurora storage in the console. What is correct?

options.A: Aurora storage auto-scales in 10 GB increments — no manual storage provisioning step
options.B: You must pre-purchase Aurora IOPS like gp3 EBS before additional writes are accepted
options.C: Storage is fixed at cluster creation; add a second cluster and shard rows by country code
options.D: Only creating manual snapshots increases usable Aurora volume size for new write traffic

questions.question: RDS PostgreSQL in us-east-1 has a cross-Region read replica in eu-west-1 for DR. The primary Region is declared lost. Leadership wants the replica to accept writes as the new production database. What action is required?

options.A: Enable Multi-AZ on the replica — AWS automatically swaps application DNS endpoints to eu-west-1
options.B: Failover the Aurora Global Database secondary with no separate promotion step required
options.C: Increase the replica instance class — promotion happens automatically on any scale-up operation
options.D: Promote the read replica to a standalone DB instance — breaks replication, becomes primary

questions.question: An exam question contrasts RDS Multi-AZ with a read replica in the same Region. Which statement is accurate?

options.A: Both use synchronous replication so reads on either endpoint remain strongly consistent always
options.B: Multi-AZ uses synchronous replication for HA; read replicas use async replication for scale
options.C: Read replicas auto-failover the primary writer; Multi-AZ is only for manual maintenance windows
options.D: Multi-AZ standby is the preferred endpoint for analytics SELECT workloads on standard RDS

questions.question: Compliance requires point-in-time recovery for a GSA RDS PostgreSQL instance with up to one month of restore granularity. Automated backups are enabled. What is the maximum automated backup retention period RDS supports?

options.A: 7 days — longer automated retention requires Aurora clusters only, not standard RDS
options.B: 14 days — cross-Region snapshot copy extends retention to 35 days automatically
options.C: 35 days — enables PITR within that window when automated backups remain enabled
options.D: 365 days — match S3 Glacier Deep Archive retention for database transaction logs

questions.question: A startup asks whether Aurora Serverless v2 can scale database capacity to zero ACUs overnight to eliminate idle cost like their old Serverless v1 dev cluster. What is accurate for v2?

options.A: Yes — v2 pauses after about 10 minutes of no connections, matching Serverless v1 behavior
options.B: Yes — but only for Aurora MySQL-compatible engines, not for Aurora PostgreSQL clusters
options.C: Only when RDS Proxy is attached — the proxy alone holds the cluster in a zero-ACU state
options.D: No — v2 keeps a configurable minimum ACU; stop/start RDS or tear down idle dev stacks

questions.question: night-16-lab will place Aurora in Night 9 private subnets. A Lambda stats function in the same VPC must connect on port 5432. Both use security groups. What ingress rule belongs on the Aurora security group?

options.A: Allow TCP 5432 from the Lambda security group ID as the inbound source
options.B: Allow TCP 5432 from 0.0.0.0/0 — Lambda ENIs have no fixed private IP addresses
options.C: Allow all traffic from the VPC CIDR — stateful return traffic handles PostgreSQL replies
options.D: No inbound rule is needed — Aurora initiates outbound connections to Lambda on port 5432

questions.question: A serverless API uses 500 concurrent Lambdas that each open a DB connection per request to RDS MySQL. Connection errors spike at peak. The team already uses Secrets Manager for credentials. Minimal-change fix?

options.A: Switch every relational table to DynamoDB on-demand to remove connection pooling needs
options.B: Deploy RDS Proxy — pool connections; Lambdas target the proxy endpoint instead of RDS
options.C: Enable Multi-AZ — doubles usable connection capacity by serving reads from the standby
options.D: Use Aurora Backtrack to rewind failed connections to a healthy point in time after errors

questions.question: A developer accidentally runs a bad UPDATE against production Aurora MySQL. Leadership wants to rewind the database to five minutes ago without restoring from a snapshot. Which Aurora capability applies?

options.A: Aurora PostgreSQL Backtrack — rewinds the shared storage volume for any Aurora engine
options.B: RDS automated backup PITR — instant in-place rewind with no restore window or new instance
options.C: Aurora Backtrack on Aurora MySQL-compatible clusters — not available on PostgreSQL
options.D: Promote a read replica from five minutes ago — replicas retain historical row versions

questions.question: GSA frontend tracks wiki page views with a simple partition key and conditional increments. No JOINs or ad-hoc SQL. Iceland pipeline stats need multi-table reports. Which pairing is best?

options.A: DynamoDB for page-view counters; Aurora for relational stats and JOIN reports
options.B: Aurora for both workloads — one cluster simplifies operations and credential rotation
options.C: DynamoDB for both — model JOINs as multiple GetItem calls for each reporting query
options.D: RDS Multi-AZ Oracle for counters; S3 objects for monthly stats without a database
